meta.title: Operation of Water Bath in Pharmaceutical Analysis Laboratory

sections.purpose: To provide controlled temperature water bath conditions for colour development reactions in colorimetric assays, heating of sample solutions, and maintenance of sample temperature during analytical procedures.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Analysis laboratory for sample preparation in colorimetric assays, dissolution medium temperature maintenance, and heating of standard solutions.
procedure: Fill the water bath with distilled water to the recommended level; switch on and set the thermostat to the required temperature.
Allow the bath to reach and stabilize at the set temperature (typically 37°C for colorimetric reactions; 37 ± 0.5°C for dissolution testing).
Verify temperature with a calibrated thermometer placed inside the bath.
Place sample containers (test tubes, beakers, volumetric flasks) in the bath using appropriate supports (tube racks, wire gauze).
Ensure sample containers are submerged to the level of the solution inside — not just the bottom.
Incubate for the specified time per the assay method.
For colorimetric assays: after colour development, remove samples promptly and measure absorbance within the specified time window.
Replenish evaporated water periodically with warm distilled water.
After use, switch off the bath and allow to cool before draining.
Clean the bath monthly with mild disinfectant and flush with distilled water.
Log temperature, duration, application, and operator name in the equipment register.
precautions: Always use distilled water — tap water mineral deposits foul the heating element.
Never allow water level to drop below the heating element — dry heating damages the element.
Use tongs or heat-resistant gloves when removing containers from hot water.
For dissolution testing baths: validate temperature uniformity (±0.5°C across all vessel positions) as per pharmacopeial requirements.
Calibrate the thermostat against a certified thermometer regularly.
Do not leave the bath on unattended at high temperature — evaporation can expose the heating element.
Drain, clean and refill with fresh water weekly during continuous use — stagnant water grows algae and supports microbial contamination.
